title: osf: sha2 0.10 → 0.11 (RustCrypto digest 0.11 line)
summary: The osf crate bumps its sha2 dependency from the 0.10 series to 0.11, which pulls the whole RustCrypto hashing stack forward one major generation: digest 0.10.7 → 0.11.3, block-buffer 0.10.4 → 0.12.1, crypto-common 0.1.7 → 0.2.2 and cpufeatures 0.2.17 → 0.3.1. The old generic-array 0.14.7 backing store is dropped entirely and replaced by hybrid-array 0.4.15, with const-oid 0.10.2 newly entering the graph as a digest dependency. Nothing in the crate's own source changes; the blast radius is the dependency graph and the compile-time API surface of the hashing primitives osf calls.

lanes.label: osf crate
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf
lanes.summary: The only workspace crate touched by this change: its manifest pins sha2 to the new major line, and its compiled code is the sole consumer of the hashing API.

lanes.label: RustCrypto hashing stack
lanes.subtitle: crates.io
lanes.summary: The sha2 implementation and the digest traits it is built on. Every crate in this lane moved a major version in lockstep.

lanes.label: Buffer backends
lanes.subtitle: array storage
lanes.summary: The fixed-size array abstraction underneath the digest traits. generic-array leaves the graph and hybrid-array takes its place.

lanes.label: Platform support
lanes.subtitle: CPU + OID
lanes.summary: Low-level helpers the hashing stack links against: CPU feature detection and the object-identifier constants digest now depends on.

nodes.label: osf
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf
nodes.summary: The workspace crate whose manifest changes. It depends on sha2 for content hashing; no source file in the crate is edited by this diff, so the change is purely which implementation of the same API it links against.

nodes.label: sha2
nodes.summary: The SHA-2 implementation. The major bump is what the manifest change requests; it is the entry point through which every other version move in this diff is reached.

nodes.label: digest
nodes.summary: The trait layer sha2 implements. Its dependency list changes shape here: generic-array and typenum drop away, const-oid is added, and crypto-common moves to 0.2.

nodes.label: crypto-common
nodes.summary: Shared trait definitions for the RustCrypto crates. It swaps generic-array and typenum for hybrid-array, which is the pivot of the whole upgrade.

nodes.label: block-buffer
nodes.summary: The block-buffering layer used by the digest implementations. Its only dependency changes from generic-array to hybrid-array.

nodes.label: hybrid-array
nodes.summary: The new fixed-size array abstraction that replaces generic-array across the hashing stack. It is the single new runtime dependency introduced by this change.

nodes.label: generic-array
nodes.summary: The previous array abstraction, removed from the lockfile. It was the shared backing store for block-buffer, crypto-common and digest, so its departure is what makes this a graph-wide swap rather than a local bump.

nodes.label: typenum
nodes.subtitle: type-level integers
nodes.summary: Type-level integer arithmetic used to express digest sizes. It survives the change, but its only remaining consumer in this subgraph is hybrid-array.

nodes.label: cpufeatures
nodes.summary: Runtime CPU feature detection that sha2 uses to select accelerated code paths. It moves a major version alongside the hashing stack.

nodes.label: const-oid
nodes.summary: Object-identifier constants newly pulled in as a direct dependency of digest 0.11. It has no dependencies of its own.

nodes.label: libc
nodes.subtitle: platform bindings
nodes.summary: Unchanged platform bindings that cpufeatures links against; included to show the version bump does not reach further down the tree.

edges.label: sha2 = "0.11"
edges.summary: The one line the diff actually changes: the osf manifest now asks for the 0.11 major line instead of 0.10. Everything else in this document follows from it.

edges.label: digest 0.11
edges.summary: sha2 0.11 is built on the 0.11 digest traits, which is why the trait crate moves with it.

edges.label: cpufeatures 0.3
edges.summary: sha2 keeps its CPU-feature detection dependency, now on the 0.3 line.

edges.label: crypto-common 0.2
edges.summary: digest 0.11 depends on the 0.2 crypto-common traits.

edges.label: const-oid 0.10
edges.summary: A new direct dependency of digest in this generation; it is the only wholly new crate besides hybrid-array.

edges.label: block-buffer 0.12
edges.summary: digest still buffers input in blocks, now via block-buffer 0.12.

edges.label: hybrid-array 0.4
edges.summary: The swap that defines this upgrade: crypto-common's array storage moves from generic-array to hybrid-array.

edges.label: hybrid-array 0.4
edges.summary: block-buffer makes the same substitution, so both consumers of the old array crate move together.

edges.label: generic-array 0.14
edges.summary: The dependency that no longer exists: crypto-common previously stored its arrays in generic-array.

edges.label: generic-array 0.14
edges.summary: block-buffer's former array dependency, likewise gone.

edges.label: typenum
edges.summary: hybrid-array keeps the type-level integer machinery, so typenum stays in the graph even though its old consumers left.

edges.label: libc
edges.summary: Unchanged: the platform bindings under cpufeatures are untouched by the version bump.

flows.title: Resolving sha2 0.11 into the osf build
flows.summary: What happens when the manifest asks for sha2 0.11: the resolver walks the new digest generation, swaps the array backend, and hands osf a hashing API whose trait bounds are expressed in hybrid-array rather than generic-array.

messages.label: require sha2 0.11
messages.note: The only authored line in the diff; the rest of the lockfile churn is the resolver's answer to it.

messages.label: hybrid-array 0.4
messages.note: Where generic-array used to sit; the trait bounds osf compiles against now name hybrid-array types.

messages.label: hashing API
messages.note: Same call surface for osf, but the underlying array types in signatures and trait bounds have changed generation.

views.title: Dependency graph after the bump
views.summary: The osf crate and the RustCrypto hashing stack it links against, showing which crates moved, which arrived and which left.

views.title: Array backend swap
views.summary: Narrowed to the substitution that drives the upgrade: generic-array out, hybrid-array in, under both block-buffer and crypto-common.

steps.heading: The manifest asks for 0.11
steps.body: One line in crates/osf/Cargo.toml moves sha2 off the 0.10 line.

steps.heading: digest moves with it
steps.body: sha2 0.11 is built on digest 0.11, which drags crypto-common and block-buffer forward.

steps.heading: The array backend is replaced
steps.body: generic-array leaves the graph and hybrid-array takes over under both consumers.

steps.heading: What osf compiles against
steps.body: The call surface is unchanged, but the array types in its trait bounds are a generation newer.
